title_en: Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. and Jiang Yang v. Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. — dispute over validity of shareholders' resolution and company capital increase
ruling_gist_en: In civil and commercial legal relations, the process by which a company, as an actor, performs legal acts can be divided into two levels: first, the stage of internal intention formation, typically manifested in resolutions of the shareholders' meeting or board of directors; second, the stage of external expression of intent, typically manifested in contracts entered into by the company with third parties. For the purposes of protecting bona fide third parties and safeguarding transaction security, even where there are defects in the internal intention formation process, the company shall be bound by its external expressions as long as there is no ground for invalidity in such external acts.

full_text_en:
Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. and Jiang Yang v.
Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd.
— dispute over validity of shareholders' resolution and company capital increase

[Ruling Summary]

1. In civil and commercial legal relations, the process by which a company, as a legal entity, implements legal acts can be divided into two levels: the first is the internal stage of forming intention, which is typically manifested as a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors; the second is the stage of expressing intention externally, which is typically manifested as a contract concluded by the company with external parties. For the purpose of protecting bona fide third parties and maintaining transactional security, where there is a defect in the process of forming internal intention within the company, the company shall be bound by its external expression of intention, provided that such external act does not constitute a ground for invalidity.

2. Pursuant to Article 35 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, when a company increases its registered capital, existing shareholders have the right to subscribe for the new capital in priority, in proportion to their paid-up capital contributions. By the nature of such right, the shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe for new capital is a right of formation. The current law does not explicitly prescribe a time limit for exercising such right. However, from the perspective of maintaining transactional security and economic stability, and taking into account the rules and characteristics of commercial conduct, a people's court should, when handling relevant cases, limit the reasonable period for exercising such right, and should not support claims for exercising the preemptive right beyond such reasonable period.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2010) Min Ti Zi No. 48

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Respondent at Second Instance): Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: Building A, Torch Tower, Mianyang High-tech Zone, Sichuan Province.
Legal Representative: Chen Mugao, Chairman.
Agent ad litem: Hua Ping, Attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xia Huimin, Attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Third Party at First Instance, Respondent at Second Instance): Fujian Gusheng Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: Rooms A-5, 6, 14th Floor, International Building, Wusi Road, Gulou District, Fuzhou, Fujian Province.
Legal Representative: Chen Mugao, Chairman.
Agent ad litem: Hua Ping, Attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xia Huimin, Attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Third Party at First Instance, Respondent at Second Instance): Chen Mugao, male, Han ethnicity, born July 16, 1947, residing at Room 405, Zuohai Mingshi Building 1, 96 Meifengzhi Road, Gulou District, Fuzhou, Fujian Province, Citizen ID Number: 352102194707160410.
Agent ad litem: Hua Ping, Attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xia Huimin, Attorney at Beijing Zhong Lun Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. Domicile: Block B, 12th Floor, Unit 1, Jinyang Apartment, 133 Changhong Avenue, Fucheng District, Mianyang City, Sichuan Province.
Legal Representative: Jiang Yang, Chairman and General Manager.
Agent ad litem: Yao Huijuan, Attorney at Beijing Dongyuan Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wu Hongshun, Attorney at Beijing Dongyuan Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Jiang Yang, male, Han ethnicity, born March 21, 1962, residing at Room 1, 4th Floor, Unit 2, Building C, Dushi Gangwan, 11 Changhong Avenue, Fucheng District, Mianyang City, Sichuan Province, Citizen ID Number: 510702196203210218.
Agent ad litem: Yao Huijuan, Attorney at Beijing Dongyuan Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Wu Hongshun, Attorney at Beijing Dongyuan Law Firm.

The applicants for retrial, Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd., Fujian Gusheng Investment Co., Ltd., and Chen Mugao, being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2006) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 515 rendered by the Sichuan High People's Court in the dispute over the validity of the shareholders' resolution and the company's capital increase with the respondents, Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd., applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2008) Min Shen Zi No. 1457 dated November 16, 2009, decided to conduct a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Zhang Yongjian, Judge Lei Jiping, and Acting Judge Liu Chongli, with Clerk Bai Xue serving as recorder. This case is now concluded.

The Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province found at the first instance: Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kechuang Company) was established in July 2001. Prior to the capital increase and share expansion of Kechuang Company in December 2003, the registered capital of the company was RMB 4,753,700. Among these, Jiang Yang's capital contribution was RMB 676,000, accounting for 14.22% of the capital contribution ratio, making him the largest shareholder of the company; Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongri Company) contributed RMB 276,000, accounting for 5.81% of the capital contribution ratio. The first chairman of the board of directors of Kechuang Company was Jiang Yang. On March 31, 2003, Kechuang Company, as Party A, Lin Daye and Chen Mugao as Party B, and the Administrative Committee of Mianyang High-tech Industrial Development Zone (hereinafter referred to as the High-tech Zone Administrative Committee) as Party C, signed a cooperation agreement for the development and construction of the Mianyang Jinjiang City Garden project (Shiqiaopu project). On July 2, 2003, a general meeting of all shareholders passed a resolution to elect Li Hong as chairman of the board of directors for a term of two years. Thereafter, Jiang Yang's role in Kechuang Company was that of a director. On December 5, 2003, Kechuang Company issued a notice convening a meeting of shareholder representatives, which mainly recorded the meeting time, location, attendees, observers, and agenda items. The meeting was scheduled for 4:00 p.m. on December 16, 2003, with the following agenda: 1. Regarding the admission of Chen Mugao as a new shareholder; 2. Regarding the internal transfer of company shares; 3. Nominations for new shareholder representatives, supervisors, and accountants of the new Kechuang Company. On the afternoon of December 16, 2003, Jiang Yang and Hongri Company's authorized representative, Chang Yi, attended the shareholders' meeting. According to the voting ballots of the meeting of shareholder representatives, Jiang Yang voted in favor of item 2 of the above three agenda items and against items 1 and 3; Hongri Company's authorized representative, Chang Yi, voted in favor of item 2 and the nomination of the new accountant, and voted against the remaining items, with a notation in the comments column stating: "First, according to Article 39, paragraph 2 of the Company Law, a specific framework plan for the capital increase should be presented. Discussion and approval should first be conducted based on the original shareholders' proportion and the proportion of the new capital to the total capital after the capital increase and share expansion. Only then should the future capital contribution be decided. Consideration should be given to the original shareholders' rights under the Company Law to invest (contribute capital)." The meeting minutes were compiled by Liang Zhouping, who served as the recorder of the meeting. Except for Jiang Yang, Hongri Company, and four shareholders who abstained from voting, the other shareholders signed the meeting minutes. The minutes recorded that 22 out of 23 expected shareholder representatives were present, and a resolution was formed by a secret ballot vote; the admission agreement with Chen Mugao was discussed, and it was agreed to admit Chen Mugao as a new shareholder (75.49% in favor, 20.03% against, 4.48% abstentions); the internal share transfer of Kechuang Company was approved (100% in favor). The minutes also recorded six suggestions regarding the cooperation method with Chen Mugao, the voting results on nominations for new shareholder representatives, supervisors, and accountants of the new Kechuang Company, and the opinion of some shareholder representatives that major shareholders should serve as company directors. Thereafter, Jiang Yang's role in Kechuang Company was that of a supervisor.

On December 18, 2003, Kechuang Company, as Party A, and Chen Mugao, as Party B, signed the "Capital Contribution Agreement," which mainly recorded: Party B agrees to the capital increase and share expansion plan approved by Party A's shareholders' meeting, i.e., Party A agrees to expand the total share capital from the original 4,753,700 shares to 10,907,500 shares. Accordingly, the 4,753,700 shares held by Party A's original shareholders account for 43.6% of the total 10,907,500 shares; Party B contributes RMB 8,000,000 at RMB 1.3 per share to subscribe for 6,153,800 shares, accounting for 56.4% of the total 10,907,500 shares; the registered capital of Kechuang Company shall be correspondingly changed to RMB 10,907,500, and the excess over the registered capital of RMB 1,846,200 shall be included as capital reserve; such capital reserve shall not be used to make up for the operating losses of the previous year, and if it is subsequently used to convert into additional shares for shareholders, the shares held by Party B shall not be entitled to such right; within seven days after the signing of this agreement, Party B shall remit RMB 8,000,000 to the designated account of Party A; within seven working days after the receipt of the funds, Party A shall be responsible for commencing the procedures for the industrial and commercial registration of changes regarding shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and the company's articles of association, and the procedures for the registration of changes with other relevant government departments, including tax authorities, shall be completed within one month; the parties agree that the RMB 8,000,000 invested by Party B shall be used specifically to pay part of the land price for the 376.65 mu of residential land in Shiqiaopu, Mianyang High-tech Zone, which Party A has already acquired through the government's auction process; after Party B's capital contribution, it is expected to initially invest RMB 30,000,000 to develop the 376.65 mu residential land project in Shiqiaopu, Mianyang High-tech Zone; the cooperation agreement signed by Party A, Party B, and the High-tech Zone Administrative Committee on March 31, 2003, shall remain in effect and have the same legal force as this agreement; this agreement is made in quadruplicate, with each party holding two copies, and shall take effect upon the signatures of both parties and the receipt of RMB 8,000,000 into the designated account. The agreement also includes provisions on the composition of the board of directors, mortgage guarantees, financial management, profit distribution, and profit and loss sharing. On December 22, 2003, Chen Mugao remitted RMB 8,000,000 as share capital into the designated account of Kechuang Company.

On December 22, 2003, Hongri Company submitted to Kechuang Company the "Report on Requesting to Act as a Subscriber for the Capital Increase and Share Expansion of Kechuang Company," which mainly stated: It asserts that Jiang Yang and Hongri Company have the right to subscribe for the new capital in priority, and they are willing to subscribe for the entire RMB 8,000,000 of new capital of Kechuang Company, either jointly by Hongri Company and Jiang Yang or by one of them, on the same terms as the capital increase and share expansion plan. On December 25, 2003, the business license of Kechuang Company issued by the industry and commerce authority recorded: Legal representative: Chen Mugao, Registered capital: RMB 10,907,500, Business term: from December 25, 2003 to December 24, 2007. The amended articles of association of Kechuang Company recorded on December 25, 2003, stated: Chen Mugao's capital contribution: RMB 6,153,800, contribution ratio: 56.42%; Jiang Yang's capital contribution: RMB 676,000, contribution ratio: 6.20%; Hongri Company's capital contribution: RMB 276,000, contribution ratio: 2.53%. On December 26, 2003, Hongri Company submitted to the Mianyang High-tech Zone Industry and Commerce Bureau the "Report Requesting Non-Registration of Changes Regarding the New Capital and Addition of New Shareholders of Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd." Thereafter, Chen Mugao managed the company as the chairman of the board of directors. On March 30, 2005, Kechuang Company applied to the industry and commerce authority for company change registration, submitting materials including a report on the registration and filing of the amendment to the articles of association, the amended articles of association, share transfer agreements, a share increase/decrease change certificate issued by Chen Mugao for the transfer of 6,143,800 shares to Fujian Gusheng Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gusheng Company), receipts, etc. The amended articles of association recorded the shareholders' names, capital contributions, and contribution ratios as: Gusheng Company: capital contribution RMB 6,153,800, contribution ratio 56.42%; Chen Mugao: capital contribution RMB 1,162,400, contribution ratio 10.66%; Jiang Yang: capital contribution RMB 676,000, contribution ratio 6.20%; Hongri Company: capital contribution RMB 276,000, contribution ratio 2.53%.

On December 12, 2005, Jiang Yang and Hongri Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting a declaration that the resolution of the shareholders' meeting of Kechuang Company held on December 16, 2003, admitting Chen Mugao as a new shareholder, be invalid; that the "Capital Contribution Agreement" signed on December 18, 2003, between Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao be invalid; that they have the preemptive right to subscribe for the RMB 8,000,000 of new capital; and that Kechuang Company bear their corresponding losses.

The Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province held at first instance: Regarding the validity of the resolution of the shareholders' meeting of Kechuang Company held on December 16, 2003, admitting Chen Mugao as a new shareholder, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang argued that it was invalid on the grounds that Kechuang Company only gave 11 days' notice to the shareholders for convening the meeting, in violation of Article 44, paragraph 1 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (1999 revision, hereinafter referred to as the 1999 Company Law), which provides that "a meeting of the shareholders' meeting shall be notified to all shareholders fifteen days before the meeting is convened," and that the notice was not clear regarding the capital increase and share expansion issue. The facts found in this case reflect that Jiang Yang held multiple roles: he was the legal representative of the plaintiff Hongri Company, and before July 2, 2003, he was the largest shareholder and chairman of Kechuang Company, and thereafter, until December 16, he was the largest shareholder and director of Kechuang Company. During Jiang Yang's tenure as chairman of Kechuang Company, the company signed a cooperation agreement with Chen Mugao and others for the Shiqiaopu project, and he also attended the shareholders' meeting on December 16, 2003, and voted on the agenda items, voting against the item "admission of Mr. Chen Mugao as a new shareholder." According to Article 39, paragraph 2 of the 1999 Company Law, which provides that "a resolution of the shareholders' meeting on increasing or decreasing the registered capital of the company, merger, division, dissolution, or change of the company's form shall be adopted by shareholders representing two-thirds or more of the voting rights," the validity of a shareholders' meeting resolution does not depend on the time and content of the notice for the meeting but on whether the shareholders' approval meets the requirements of the Company Law. The facts found show that the resolution on "admission of Mr. Chen Mugao as a new shareholder" on December 16, 2003, which involved the capital increase of RMB 8,000,000 for Kechuang Company and that such increase was subscribed by Chen Mugao, was adopted by shareholders representing 75.49% of the voting rights at the shareholders' meeting. Therefore, the resolution on "admission of Mr. Chen Mugao as a new shareholder" complies with the above provisions and is valid. The arguments of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang that the resolution was invalid due to non-compliance with the notice time requirements and the content not following the discussion procedures are untenable.

Regarding the validity of the "Capital Contribution Agreement" signed on December 18, 2003, between Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao. Hongri Company and Jiang Yang argued that the agreement was signed by Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao in malicious collusion to harm their interests as shareholders. However, based on the facts found by the court of first instance, they did not provide evidence to prove the existence of such fact. During the trial, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang also raised an objection that the change registration of Kechuang Company with the industry and commerce bureau on December 25, 2005, was not genuine. This concerns the legality of the specific administrative act of the industry and commerce bureau, which is a separate legal relationship and does not fall within the scope of this case. Upon review, the parties to the "Capital Contribution Agreement" have legal capacity, the expression of intention is genuine, and the agreement does not violate the law or public interest. Therefore, it should be a valid agreement. Consequently, the claim of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang that the "Capital Contribution Agreement" is invalid is untenable.

Regarding whether Hongri Company and Jiang Yang can exercise the preemptive right to subscribe for the new capital of RMB 8,000,000 approved by the shareholders' meeting of Kechuang Company on December 16, 2003, and whether Kechuang Company should bear corresponding losses. According to Article 33 of the 1999 Company Law, which provides that "shareholders shall distribute dividends in proportion to their capital contributions. When the company increases its capital, shareholders may have the preemptive right to subscribe for the new capital," Jiang Yang and Hongri Company, as shareholders of Kechuang Company, have the preemptive right to subscribe for the new capital. However, the 1999 Company Law does not specify the period for exercising the preemptive right. Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (I), effective May 9, 2006, provides: "If a dispute arises from a civil act or event occurring before the implementation of the Company Law and is brought to a people's court, if there are no explicit provisions in the laws, regulations, or judicial interpretations at that time, the relevant provisions of the Company Law may be applied by reference." The revised Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the New Company Law), effective in 2005, also does not specify the period for exercising the preemptive right. However, Article 75, paragraph 1 of the New Company Law provides that "under any of the following circumstances, a shareholder who voted against the resolution of the shareholders' meeting may request the company to repurchase its shares at a reasonable price," and paragraph 2 provides that "if the shareholder and the company fail to reach an agreement on the share repurchase within sixty days from the date of adoption of the shareholders' meeting resolution, the shareholder may file a lawsuit with a people's court within ninety days from the date of adoption of the shareholders' meeting resolution." Although this article addresses the right of dissenting shareholders to request share repurchase, in accordance with the spirit of civil law, from the perspective of the reciprocal relationship between the company's repurchase of shares from shareholders and the shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe for new capital, the latter should also have a reasonable period for exercise to ensure transactional security and fairness. The facts found in this case show that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang claimed the preemptive right to subscribe for the new capital of RMB 8,000,000 from Kechuang Company on December 22, 2003, but did not file a lawsuit until December 12, 2005. During this period, Chen Mugao transferred shares representing 56.42% of the capital contribution ratio to Gusheng Company, and he successively signed share transfer agreements with other shareholders, all of which were registered for changes. From December 25, 2003, Chen Mugao has served as the chairman of Kechuang Company, and the outlook for Kechuang Company's Shiqiaopu project has become clear. Therefore, it is unreasonable that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang filed the lawsuit only on December 12, 2005. The shareholders' meeting resolution of December 16, 2003, and the "Capital Contribution Agreement" are lawful and valid. The reasonable period for Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to exercise the preemptive right has passed. Therefore, their request for the preemptive right to subscribe for the RMB 8,000,000 capital and for compensation for their losses is not supported.

In conclusion, the shareholders' meeting resolution of December 16, 2003, and the "Capital Contribution Agreement" are lawful and valid. When Hongri Company and Jiang Yang claimed the preemptive right from Kechuang Company on December 22, 2003, the above two agreements had already taken effect and were in the process of being performed. However, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang did not take timely further legal measures to realize their preemptive right. Prior to the filing of this lawsuit, a series of new civil and administrative relationships had arisen around Kechuang Company and its equity, forming a series of new transactional relationships. To protect transactional security, the claims of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang in this case cannot be sustained. Accordingly, the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province, by civil judgment (2006) Mian Min Chu Zi No. 2, ruled: reject all claims of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang. The court acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 50,010, and other litigation costs were RMB 25,005, totaling RMB 75,015, to be borne jointly by Hongri Company and Jiang Yang.

Hongri Company and Jiang Yang, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court, arguing: that Kechuang Company's notice of the shareholders' meeting given only 11 days in advance violated the mandatory statutory obligation under the Company Law to provide 15 days' notice; that the notice did not include the specific plan for the company's capital increase and share expansion or the draft of the "Share Subscription Agreement"; that the vote at the shareholders' meeting was a surprise attack, and the议事 procedures were illegal; that at the shareholders' meeting, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang voted against the proposal, stating that they agreed to a capital increase of RMB 8 million but did not waive their preemptive subscription rights; that the shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase of RMB 8 million was valid, but the resolution to admit Chen Mugao as a new shareholder and the "Share Subscription Agreement" were invalid because they infringed upon their preemptive subscription rights; that the Company Law does not provide for a statute of limitations for shareholders to exercise their preemptive subscription rights, and the two-year statute of limitations under the General Principles of the Civil Law should apply; that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang became aware of the infringement of their rights on December 22, 2003, and the statute of limitations ran from that date until December 22, 2005; that this lawsuit was filed on December 12, 2005, and thus did not exceed the statute of limitations; that the first-instance judgment erroneously applied the 90-day period stipulated in the Company Law for company repurchases of shareholders' shares; that Chen Mugao was the legal representative of Gusheng Company, and Gusheng Company did not acquire the shares in good faith, and its shareholder status was also illegal, so there was no issue of protecting transaction security. They requested the second-instance court to set aside the original judgment and enter a judgment in accordance with the law.

The appellees, Kechuang Company, Gusheng Company, and Chen Mugao, argued in response: that although the procedure for convening the shareholders' meeting by Kechuang Company did not comply with the Company Law requirement of 15 days' advance notice, that provision is a permissive norm, and all shareholders attended on time, so it does not affect the validity of the resolution; that the meaning of "admitting Mr. Chen Mugao as a new shareholder" proposed by Kechuang Company was a定向 capital increase and share expansion, and this agenda item was passed by shareholders representing more than two-thirds of the voting rights; that Chen Mugao exercised reasonable care, and according to Article 39 of the 1999 Company Law, the resolution on this agenda item was legally valid; that when a company increases its capital and expands its shares, it enters into a share subscription agreement with the new shareholder, and there is no prohibition in the law, and this represents the will of the vast majority of shareholders and does not violate Article 33 of the 1999 Company Law; that by the time Hongri Company and Jiang Yang raised their claim for preemptive subscription, the "Share Subscription Agreement" had already been formed and was in the process of being performed, so it should be valid; that Kechuang Company admitted Chen Mugao as a shareholder because the company was facing the difficulty of being unable to pay the land price, and the land would be taken back by the government; that Chen Mugao contributed RMB 8 million, purchased shares at a premium of RMB 1.3 per share, and promised that after becoming a new shareholder, he would no longer share the 35% profit that Kechuang Company was entitled to under the cooperative project agreement; that this resolution maximized the company's interests and protected the interests of the original shareholders; that Chen Mugao later transferred the shares to Gusheng Company by way of gift and transfer, and both Chen Mugao and Gusheng Company were bona fide third parties; that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang participated in multiple board meetings and shareholders' meetings chaired by Chen Mugao over a period of two years without taking further legal action regarding their preemptive subscription rights, but filed this lawsuit when the company began to improve, lacking reasonableness and legitimacy. They requested the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The Sichuan High People's Court confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court and supplemented the following facts: In July 2001, Kechuang Company was established with registered capital of RMB 1.56 million and 20 shareholders, all natural persons. Jiang Yang contributed RMB 520,000, representing 33.33% of the capital, and served as chairman of the board. On January 20, 2003, Kechuang Company acquired through a listing-for-sale process a 325-mu residential project site in the Shiqiao Pu International Investment Zone, Mianyang High-tech Zone, but failed to pay the land transfer fee and did not obtain a land use certificate. On March 31, 2003, Kechuang Company entered into a Shiqiao Pu project cooperation agreement with Lin Daye, Chen Mugao, and the Management Committee of the High-tech Zone, stipulating that Kechuang Company would pay the land price and Chen Mugao would provide the project development funds and construction. In September of the same year, the chairman of Kechuang Company was changed to Li Hong, the registered capital was increased by RMB 3.1937 million to RMB 4.7537 million, and the shareholders were changed to 23 parties, including two additional natural person shareholders and one legal person shareholder, Hongri Company. Jiang Yang's capital contribution was changed from RMB 520,000 to RMB 676,000, reducing his shareholding ratio to 14.22%, and Hongri Company made a new contribution of RMB 276,000, representing 5.81% of the capital. Kechuang Company's articles of association provided: that when the company increases its capital, shareholders have the right to preemptively subscribe for the new capital; that the company shall notify all shareholders 15 days before convening a shareholders' meeting, with the notice sent in writing and stating the time, place, and content of the meeting; and that the shareholders' meeting shall make resolutions on the increase or decrease of the company's registered capital. On December 16 of the same year, Kechuang Company held a shareholders' meeting, discussed the "Share Subscription Agreement" concerning Chen Mugao's capital contribution, and passed a proposal to admit Chen Mugao as a new shareholder. Jiang Yang and Hongri Company voted against the proposal. On December 18 of the same year, Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao signed the "Share Subscription Agreement," stipulating that Chen Mugao would contribute RMB 8 million to subscribe 6.1538 million shares at RMB 1.3 per share. On December 22 of the same year, Chen Mugao remitted RMB 8 million to Kechuang Company's account as payment for land, and Hongri Company demanded preemptive subscription of the new capital. On December 25 of the same year, Kechuang Company changed its legal representative to Chen Mugao, and the registered capital increased to RMB 10.9075 million, with Chen Mugao holding 56.4%. On December 26, 2003, Kechuang Company paid the land price of RMB 8 million. On March 5, 2004, Kechuang Company paid the entire land price of RMB 13,020,175 and obtained the land use certificate. On February 1, 2005, Kechuang Company held a shareholders' meeting and passed a resolution approving Chen Mugao's gift of 10,000 shares to Gusheng Company. Hongri Company and Jiang Yang attended the meeting and abstained from voting. On March 1 of the same year, Chen Mugao transferred 6.1438 million shares to Gusheng Company, which then held a total of 6.1538 million shares in Kechuang Company. From February 2005 to November 2006, Chen Mugao purchased 3.1571 million shares from other natural person shareholders at RMB 1.2 per share. Kechuang Company's shareholders became: Gusheng Company, 6.1538 million shares (56.42%); Chen Mugao, 3.1571 million shares (28.94%); Jiang Yang, 676,000 shares (6.20%); Hongri Company, 276,000 shares (2.53%); and 11 other natural person shareholders, totaling 644,600 shares (5.91%). At present, the Shiqiao Pu project that Kechuang Company plans to develop has only built a 200-meter cement road from the city highway to the project site, and the entire project has not yet started due to issues such as relocation and planning.

The Sichuan High People's Court held in the second instance: The resolution passed at Kechuang Company's shareholders' meeting on December 16, 2003, regarding "admitting Mr. Chen Mugao as a new shareholder," when read together with the "Share Subscription Agreement" discussed at the meeting, included two aspects: a capital increase of RMB 8 million by Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao becoming a new shareholder of Kechuang Company by subscribing to the RMB 8 million new capital. According to Article 38, Paragraph 1, Item (8) of the 1999 Company Law, which provides that "the shareholders' meeting shall exercise the function and power to adopt resolutions on increasing or reducing the registered capital of the company," and Article 39, Paragraph 2, which provides that "resolutions of the shareholders' meeting on increasing or reducing the registered capital, merger, division, dissolution, or change of the company form must be adopted by shareholders representing more than two-thirds of the voting rights," the resolution to increase Kechuang Company's capital by RMB 8 million was passed by shareholders representing 75.49% of the voting rights and thus should be lawful and valid. According to Article 33 of the 1999 Company Law, which provides that "when the company increases its capital, shareholders may preemptively subscribe for the new capital," and the same provision in Kechuang Company's articles of association, the original shareholders, Jiang Yang and Hongri Company, had the preemptive subscription right for this capital increase. At the shareholders' meeting, Jiang Yang and Hongri Company voted against the agenda item of having Chen Mugao subscribe to the RMB 8 million new capital and become a new shareholder, and wrote the comment that "the original shareholders' investment (subscription) rights under the Company Law should be considered." This was their expression of opposition to Chen Mugao subscribing to the new capital and becoming a shareholder, and their indication that the company should consider their preemptive subscription rights as original shareholders, clearly stating that they did not waive their preemptive subscription rights. Subsequently, on December 22 and 26 of the same year, Jiang Yang and Hongri Company respectively submitted to Kechuang Company a "Report on Requesting to Act as the Subscriber for the Capital Increase and Share Expansion of Kechuang Company" and submitted to the Mianyang High-tech Zone Industrial and Commercial Bureau a "Report Requesting Not to Make Changes in Registration for the New Capital and New Shareholder of Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd.," further unequivocally asserting their preemptive subscription rights. The above facts all demonstrate that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang never waived their preemptive subscription rights. However, without appropriately consulting Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to ascertain whether they would waive their preemptive subscription rights, and without granting them a reasonable period to exercise those rights, Kechuang Company signed the "Share Subscription Agreement" with Chen Mugao on December 18 of the same year, and on December 25, changed the industrial and commercial registration, changing the legal representative to Chen Mugao and increasing the company's registered capital to RMB 10.9075 million, with the new capital of RMB 6.1538 million registered under Chen Mugao's name. This series of actions infringed upon the preemptive subscription rights that Jiang Yang and Hongri Company enjoyed under the law with respect to the new capital of Kechuang Company. Pursuant to Article 58, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, which provides that "civil acts that violate the law or the public interest are void," the portion of the shareholders' resolution concerning Chen Mugao's subscription of the new capital of RMB 8 million and his resulting status as a shareholder of Kechuang Company was void, and the "Share Subscription Agreement" signed between Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao was correspondingly void. Although the shareholders' resolution in question was passed by shareholders representing more than two-thirds of the voting rights, the preemptive right of original shareholders to subscribe to new capital is a statutory right of individual original shareholders and cannot be deprived by a majority vote of the shareholders' meeting. Therefore, the grounds of appeal raised by Jiang Yang and Hongri Company that the portion of the shareholders' resolution concerning the admission of Chen Mugao as a shareholder and the "Share Subscription Agreement" were void, and that they had the preemptive right to subscribe to Kechuang Company's new capital of RMB 8 million, were established in law, and the second-instance court supported them.

Pursuant to Article 61 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, where a civil act is confirmed to be void or is rescinded, the property obtained by the parties as a result of such act shall be returned to the party that suffered the loss. Therefore, the shares obtained by Chen Mugao under the void portion of the resolution and the "Share Subscription Agreement" should be returned. Although Chen Mugao later gifted and transferred his shares to Gusheng Company, Chen Mugao was the legal representative of Gusheng Company, and Gusheng Company knew or should have known that Chen Mugao's subscription of the new capital infringed upon others' preemptive subscription rights. Therefore, Gusheng Company did not acquire the shares in good faith, and the gift and transfer between them were also void. Gusheng Company should return the 6.1538 million shares it held in Kechuang Company to Kechuang Company, to be subscribed for by Hongri Company and Jiang Yang pursuant to their preemptive rights. Kechuang Company should return the RMB 8 million subscription funds and corresponding interest thereon to Chen Mugao.

Regarding the statute of limitations for a limited liability company shareholder to seek judicial protection of their preemptive right to subscribe to new capital, there is no special provision in current law. The two-year general statute of limitations under the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC should apply. Jiang Yang and Hongri Company submitted a written request to preemptively subscribe to the new capital of RMB 8 million on December 22, 2003, and filed this lawsuit on December 19, 2005. This is within the two-year statute of limitations provided by that law. Their claim for preemptive subscription of the RMB 8 million new capital was established in law, and the second-instance court supported it. The request by Jiang Yang and Hongri Company that Kechuang Company should bear their corresponding losses was not supported by evidence, and the second-instance court did not support it. The first-instance judgment had unclear fact-finding and erroneous application of law, and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, Article 33, Article 38, Paragraph 1, Item (8), and Article 39, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law of the PRC (1999 Revision), and Article 58, Paragraph 1, Items (4) and (5), Article 61, and Article 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, and after discussion by the Adjudication Committee of the second-instance court, it was decided as follows: 1. The civil judgment (2006)Mian Min Chu Zi No. 2 of the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province was set aside; 2. The portion of the shareholders' resolution of Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. dated December 16, 2003, concerning the admission of Chen Mugao as a shareholder, is void; 3. The "Share Subscription Agreement" signed between Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. and Chen Mugao on December 18, 2003, is void; 4. Jiang Yang and Mianyang Hongri Industry Co., Ltd. have the preemptive right to purchase the 6.1538 million shares newly issued by Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. as decided at the shareholders' meeting on December 16, 2003, for RMB 8 million; 5. Jiang Yang and Mianyang Hongri Industry Co., Ltd. shall pay the RMB 8 million share purchase payment to Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. within 15 days after this judgment takes effect; 6. Within 15 days after Jiang Yang and Mianyang Hongri Industry Co., Ltd. perform the fifth item of this judgment, Fujian Gusheng Investment Co., Ltd. shall return the 6.1538 million shares it holds in Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. to the company, and accordingly, Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. shall register that portion of shares under the names of Jiang Yang and Mianyang Hongri Industry Co., Ltd. based on their subscription intent and payment; 7. Within 3 days after Fujian Gusheng Investment Co., Ltd. performs the sixth item of this judgment, Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd. shall return RMB 8 million plus interest (calculated from December 23, 2003, to the date of full payment at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for circulating funds of the same period) to Chen Mugao; 8. The other claims of Jiang Yang and Mianyang Hongri Industry Co., Ltd. are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee was RMB 75,015, the second-instance case acceptance fee was RMB 75,015, and the preservation fee was RMB 5,000, all to be borne by Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industry Co., Ltd.

Kechuang Company, Gusheng Company, and Chen Mugao, dissatisfied with the above second-instance civil judgment of the Sichuan High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: 1. The findings of fact in the second-instance judgment lack evidentiary support. The shareholders' resolution of Kechuang Company dated December 16, 2003, "concerning admitting Chen Mugao as a new shareholder," and the "Share Subscription Agreement" signed between Chen Mugao and Kechuang Company on December 18, 2003, are both lawful and valid. a. The second-instance court incorrectly split the content of the shareholders' resolution into two parts: "Kechuang Company increases capital by RMB 8 million" and "Chen Mugao becomes a new shareholder of Kechuang Company by subscribing to the RMB 8 million new capital." This is seriously inconsistent with the facts. These two items are inseparable; the capital increase of RMB 8 million was predicated on admitting Chen Mugao as a new shareholder. b. The comment written by Hongri Company on the opposition ballot cannot be interpreted as an expression of not waiving its preemptive subscription rights. The comment cited Article 39, Paragraph 2 of the 1999 Company Law, which concerns the voting procedure for resolutions on capital increase or reduction, and is unrelated to the preemptive subscription right under Article 33. Furthermore, the report submitted by Hongri Company on December 22, 2003, did not bear Jiang Yang's signature, so it cannot be considered that Jiang Yang asserted his preemptive right. c. The preemptive subscription right is a formative right, and its exercise should have a reasonable period. Kechuang Company admitted Chen Mugao's capital contribution under the urgent circumstance of needing to pay the land transfer fee for the Shiqiao Pu project. The period for Jiang Yang and Hongri Company to exercise their preemptive subscription rights should not exceed the final deadline for Kechuang Company to pay the land transfer fee, i.e., December 31, 2003. d. Gusheng Company and Chen Mugao did not act in bad faith in acquiring shares in Kechuang Company, and there was no malicious collusion when signing the "Share Subscription Agreement." 2. The second-instance judgment erroneously applied the law. The second-instance court applied Article 58, Paragraph 1, Items (4) and (5) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, but there was no evidence proving malicious collusion between Chen Mugao and Kechuang Company or that the "Share Subscription Agreement" violated the law or public interest. Citing those provisions to declare the shareholders' resolution and the "Share Subscription Agreement" void was a clear error in applying the law. Consequently, the court's citation of Article 61 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and Article 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC was also inconsistent with the facts. Even if Jiang Yang and Hongri Company's claim to exercise preemptive subscription rights could be upheld, under Article 2 of the Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the PRC (I) and Article 35 of the new Company Law, they could only subscribe to the new capital in proportion to their actual paid-in capital contributions, not subscribe to the entire RMB 8 million new capital. Furthermore, the second-instance court's application of the two-year general statute of limitations under the General Principles of the Civil Law was also erroneous. The shareholders' preemptive subscription right is a formative right and should be subject to a limitation period, not exceeding one year. 3. After Chen Mugao's capital contribution to Kechuang Company, he invested substantial funds and wisdom, resulting in significant progress in the company's management and the Shiqiao Pu project. The equity value of Kechuang Company has greatly increased, far exceeding the purchase price at that time. The second-instance judgment, without reassessing the equity value, allowed Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to purchase the equity at the 2003 price, which violates the principle of fairness. In summary, they requested that the civil judgment (2006)Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 515 of the Sichuan High People's Court be set aside, the civil judgment (2006)Mian Min Chu Zi No. 2 of the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court be affirmed, the enforcement of the civil judgment (2006)Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 515 of the Sichuan High People's Court be stayed, and all first-instance and second-instance litigation costs be borne by the respondents, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang.

Respondents Hongri Company and Jiang Yang argued in defense: The facts found in the first-instance and second-instance judgments were clear, and the evidence was conclusive. The resolution to "admit Chen Mugao as a new shareholder" was not made under the severe circumstances where the company faced inability to pay and the land would be reclaimed. Hongri Company and Jiang Yang were fully capable at that time of increasing capital and expanding shares to pay off the land transfer fees; the reason for non-payment was that there were still multiple unsettled accounts between Kechuang Company and the Administrative Committee of the High-tech Zone. The resolution to "admit Chen Mugao as a new shareholder" could be understood as having two components: "Kechuang Company increases its capital by RMB 8 million" and "Chen Mugao becomes a new shareholder of Kechuang Company by subscribing to the newly increased capital of RMB 8 million." The votes cast by Hongri Company and Jiang Yang against the resolution, along with their endorsements, indicated their agreement to "Kechuang Company increases its capital by RMB 8 million" but opposition to "Chen Mugao becoming a new shareholder of Kechuang Company by subscribing to the newly increased capital of RMB 8 million." Even if Hongri Company and Jiang Yang opposed both components, it would not affect the legal validity of "Kechuang Company increases its capital by RMB 8 million." The passage of the capital increase and share expansion resolution by a majority vote complied with the provisions of the 1999 Company Law and did not infringe upon the original shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe for capital contributions. Only the part concerning "Chen Mugao becoming a new shareholder of Kechuang Company by subscribing to the newly increased capital of RMB 8 million" infringed upon the original shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe for capital contributions. The endorsement on the voting slip by Hongri Company clearly indicated that the capital increase must be carried out in accordance with Article 39, Paragraph 2 of the 1999 Company Law, and that Article 33 should be considered regarding the original shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe for capital contributions, demonstrating that Hongri Company had not waived its preemptive right. Hongri Company and Jiang Yang only learned on the day of the shareholders' meeting that Kechuang Company was about to increase its capital and expand shares by RMB 8 million. Therefore, the period for exercising their preemptive right to subscribe for shares should be a reasonable period commencing from December 16, 2003, not a requirement to exercise the right on that same day. On December 22, 2003, Hongri Company submitted a "Report on Request to Act as a Subscriber for the Capital Increase and Share Expansion of Kechuang Company" to Kechuang Company, expressing its intention to exercise the preemptive right to subscribe. This time was earlier than the effective date stipulated in the "Capital Contribution Agreement" signed between Chen Mugao and Kechuang Company. Chen Mugao, knowing that the original shareholders of Kechuang Company had the ability to subscribe for the newly increased capital and had claimed their preemptive right, nonetheless entered into the "Capital Contribution Agreement" with Kechuang Company, which clearly infringed upon the preemptive rights of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang. The provisions in the "Capital Contribution Agreement" concerning the composition of the new board of directors of the company, the appointment of Chen Mugao as chairman and general manager, the investment issues of the new RMB 8 million capital, the arrangement of financial personnel, and profit distribution all violated Article 37, Article 38, Article 46 of the Company Law and Article 24 of Kechuang Company's articles of association. These provisions exceeded the authority and exercised statutory powers belonging to the shareholders' meeting and the board of directors, and therefore should also be deemed invalid according to law. Gusheng Company was established with capital from Chen Mugao and his family members, and Chen Mugao serves as its legal representative. Thus, this company can be considered Chen Mugao's own company. The shares Chen Mugao obtained in Kechuang Company were unlawful, and his transfer of the shares constituted unauthorized disposition. Gusheng Company, as Chen Mugao's personal company, obviously acted in bad faith in accepting the transferred equity. Second, the second-instance judgment correctly applied the law. Article 58, Item (4) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China should be understood as follows: as long as the actor was aware that the act might infringe upon the interests of a third party and intentionally proceeded, it constitutes malicious intent. Before convening the shareholders' meeting on December 16, 2003, Kechuang Company had already reached the "Capital Contribution Agreement" and a draft contract for management and operation with Chen Mugao. Moreover, when signing the "Capital Contribution Agreement," Chen Mugao was also aware that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang opposed his becoming a new shareholder of Kechuang Company. Therefore, the "Capital Contribution Agreement" signed between Chen Mugao and Kechuang Company should be considered an act of malicious collusion. If the preemptive right to subscribe is considered a formative right, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang had already exercised that right on December 22, 2003. When this right was infringed, the two-year ordinary statute of limitations for litigation should apply. Third, since Chen Mugao entered Kechuang Company, he has basically made no investment, the company's assets have basically not increased, and the company's Shiqiaopu project has remained largely undeveloped. Chen Mugao's actions have caused dissatisfaction among local residents and a series of social problems. In summary, the second-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. The reasons for the retrial application of the applicants for retrial are untenable and should be dismissed according to law.

During the retrial, respondents Hongri Company and Jiang Yang submitted evidentiary materials including a notarized letter of demand, enforcement documents from the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court, a notarized deposit, and a notarized record of the 2008 extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Kechuang Company. These were used to demonstrate the implementation after the second-instance judgment and the current shareholding structure of Kechuang Company. They also submitted materials on Kechuang Company's operating conditions from 2004 to 2008, materials on the demolition compensation for villagers involved in the Shiqiaopu project, and a joint letter from villagers, to prove that Chen Mugao made no investment in Kechuang Company after entering it and that Kechuang Company made new investments in the Shiqiaopu project after Hongri Company and Jiang Yang obtained the new shares.

The applicants for retrial, Kechuang Company, Gusheng Company, and Chen Mugao, challenged the evidence, arguing that the notarized letter of demand, the enforcement documents from the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court, the notarized deposit, and the notarized record of the 2008 extraordinary shareholders' meeting all occurred after the second-instance judgment and were irrelevant to the dispute in this case. The industrial and commercial registration materials were not new evidence. They also objected to the authenticity, relevance to this case, and the content of the materials on demolition compensation for villagers and the joint letter.

After the retrial, this Court confirms the facts found by the lower courts.

This Court holds: Based on the facts of this case and the contentions of both parties, the following two issues are in dispute in this retrial procedure: First, whether the shareholders' resolution of Kechuang Company dated December 16, 2003, and the "Capital Contribution Agreement" between Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao dated December 18, 2003, are valid; Second, whether Hongri Company and Jiang Yang can exercise the preemptive right to subscribe for the 6,153,800 new shares of Kechuang Company issued in 2003.

Regarding the first issue. When Kechuang Company adopted the shareholders' resolution on December 16, 2003, the current Company Law had not yet taken effect. According to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (I), where the laws and judicial interpretations in effect at that time had no explicit provisions, the current Company Law may be applied by reference. Article 33 of the Company Law provides: "Where a company increases its capital, its shareholders have the preemptive right to subscribe for the newly issued capital on a pro rata basis." According to Article 35 of the current Company Law, when a company increases its capital, the shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe should be limited to their respective paid-in capital contribution ratios. The shareholders' resolution adopted by Kechuang Company on December 16, 2003, without giving Hongri Company and Jiang Yang the option to exercise their preemptive right to subscribe in proportion to their respective paid-in capital contributions, and despite their explicit opposition, directly passed by a majority vote the resolution for a third party, Chen Mugao, to subscribe for all 6,153,800 new shares of Kechuang Company by contributing RMB 8 million. This infringed upon the right of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to preemptively subscribe for new capital in proportion to their respective capital contributions, in violation of the above legal provisions. Article 22, Paragraph 1 of the current Company Law provides: "A resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders, or of the board of directors, that violates any law or administrative regulation shall be void." According to the above provisions, regarding the resolution content adopted at the Kechuang Company shareholders' meeting on December 16, 2003, that Chen Mugao would subscribe for 6,153,800 new shares of Kechuang Company by contributing RMB 8 million, the parts involving 14.22% and 5.81% of the new shares are void because they respectively infringed upon the preemptive right of Jiang Yang and Hongri Company. The part involving 79.97% of the new shares is valid because other shareholders, by voting in favor or abstaining, waived their preemptive right. The civil judgment (2006) Mian Min Chu Zi No. 2 of the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province, which held the entire resolution valid, was incorrect and should be corrected. The shareholders' meeting listed "admitting Chen Mugao as a new shareholder" as an agenda item, but this item actually contained two aspects: increasing capital by RMB 8 million and having Chen Mugao subscribe for the new capital contribution. The invalidity of the part of the resolution concerning Chen Mugao's subscription for the new capital contribution does not affect the validity of the capital increase resolution. Kechuang Company's argument that the two aspects are inseparable lacks basis and is not supported by this Court.

The "Capital Contribution Agreement" signed between Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao on December 18, 2003, is a contract between Kechuang Company and a third party outside the company. The general principles of contract law and relevant legal provisions should be applied to determine its validity. Although the shareholders' resolution adopted by Kechuang Company on December 16, 2003, was partially invalid, causing a defect in the intent of Kechuang Company in reaching the above agreement, Chen Mugao, as the counterparty to the contract, had no obligation to review the process of Kechuang Company's formation of intent. Kechuang Company's external agreements should be governed by its expressed conduct. The above "Capital Contribution Agreement" represents the mutual expression of intent of Kechuang Company and Chen Mugao, does not violate any mandatory legal prohibitions of the state, and Chen Mugao paid the corresponding consideration in accordance with the agreement. There is no evidence that the parties colluded maliciously to harm the interests of others. Therefore, the agreement does not fall under any of the circumstances rendering a contract void as provided in Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and should be valid. The "Capital Contribution Agreement" contains provisions on the composition of the new board of directors of Kechuang Company and the selection of the chairman and general manager, but these provisions do not preclude Kechuang Company from making decisions internally in accordance with the voting procedures stipulated by law and its articles of association, and thus do not render the contract invalid. The second-instance court's determination that the "Capital Contribution Agreement" was void based on Article 58, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China was an error in the application of law and is hereby corrected by this Court.

Regarding the second issue. Although the shareholders' resolution of Kechuang Company dated December 16, 2003, is partially invalid because it infringed upon the right of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to preemptively subscribe for new capital in proportion to their respective paid-in capital contributions, whether Hongri Company and Jiang Yang can exercise the preemptive right to subscribe for the above new capital also requires consideration of whether they properly asserted their right. The shareholders' preemptive right to subscribe for a company's new capital is a formative right. Although the current law does not explicitly stipulate a period for exercising this right, to safeguard transaction security and stabilize the economic order, this right should be exercised within a certain reasonable period. Moreover, because the exercise of this right is a typical commercial act, the determination of a reasonable period should be stricter than for ordinary civil acts. In this case, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang knew that their preemptive right to subscribe had been infringed upon at the shareholders' meeting of Kechuang Company on December 16, 2003, and expressed their intention to exercise that right. However, they did not take timely action, such as filing a lawsuit, to actively assert their right. Thereafter, when Kechuang Company convened a shareholders' meeting and passed a resolution on Chen Mugao's proposal to donate part of his equity to Gusheng Company, Hongri Company and Jiang Yang attended the meeting and did not object. Hongri Company and Jiang Yang filed a lawsuit nearly two years after the equity change. By that time, the value of the disputed equity had changed significantly. Allowing them to exercise the preemptive right to subscribe for capital contributions at this point would disrupt the already stabilized legal relationship and could easily lead to a result that is clearly unfair. Therefore, the civil judgment (2006) Mian Min Chu Zi No. 2 of the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province correctly found that the reasonable period for Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to assert their preemptive right had expired. Accordingly, this Court does not support the request of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang to exercise the preemptive right to subscribe for Kechuang Company's new capital.

Hongri Company and Jiang Yang requested in their first-instance claims that Kechuang Company bear their corresponding losses, but they did not specify the amount of compensation claimed, nor did they submit evidence to prove such losses. This Court does not address this claim. During the retrial, the Hongri Company party argued that they had made investments in Kechuang Company based on the new equity. This claim is not within the scope of this trial; they may file a separate lawsuit for this matter.

In summary, the claims of Hongri Company and Jiang Yang are partially established. However, the civil judgment (2006) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 515 of the Sichuan High People's Court, which held that Hongri Company and Jiang Yang could exercise the preemptive right to subscribe for the 6,153,800 new shares of Kechuang Company issued in 2003, lacked sufficient factual basis and was an improper application of law. This judgment should be reversed. Pursuant to Article 186 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby orders:

1. The civil judgment (2006) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 515 of the Sichuan High People's Court and the civil judgment (2006) Mian Min Chu Zi No. 2 of the Mianyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province are both reversed;

2. Regarding the resolution content adopted at the shareholders' meeting of Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. on December 16, 2003, that Chen Mugao would subscribe for 6,153,800 new shares of Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. by contributing RMB 8 million, the part involving 20.03% of the new shares is void, and the part involving 79.97% of the new shares and the other content of the resolution are valid;

3. The other claims of Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. and Jiang Yang are dismissed.

First-instance case acceptance fee: RMB 75,015; preservation fee: RMB 5,000; total: RMB 80,015. Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 37,507.5; Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. and Jiang Yang shall bear RMB 42,507.5. Second-instance case acceptance fee: RMB 75,015. Mianyang High-tech Zone Kechuang Industrial Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 37,507.5; Mianyang Hongri Industrial Co., Ltd. and Jiang Yang shall bear RMB 37,507.5.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Yongjian

Judge: Lei Jiping

Acting Judge: Liu Chongli
